tool.name: Figaro
tool.description: Determine optimal truncation parameters for amplicon sequencing data

param.name: input_collection
param.label: Select your paired collection to analyze

param.help: Minimum overlap between the paired-end reads.

param.name: percentile
param.label: Percentile
param.help: Percentile to use for expected error model.

tool.help:
What it does ------------ Figaro analyzes paired-end sequencing reads to determine the optimal truncation parameters for DADA2 denoising, maximizing the number of reads that successfully overlap.
Inputs ------ - **Input FASTQ files**: Paired-end raw or trimmed reads with consistent read length in a collection. - **Amplicon Length**: The expected length of the amplicon excluding primers. - **Primer Lengths**: The exact lengths of the forward and reverse primers.
Outputs ----- - **png**: forwardExpectedError.png and reverseExpectedError.png. Figaro tool only produces the forward and reverse png of the final paired-end data. - **json**: trimParameters.json - **log**: standard output
**NOTE:** The input paired-end dataset should be uncompressed paired-end dataset and in a collection. Please see `Creating a paired collection`_.
For more information please look at the `github repository`_ and tutorial_.
.. _github repository: https://github.com/Zymo-Research/figaro .. _tutorial: https://nuriamw.github.io/micro4all/tutorial/package_workflow.html#figaro-selection-of-trimming-parameters .. _Creating a paired collection: https://training.galaxyproject.org/training-material/faqs/galaxy/collections_build_list_paired.html
